case_notes.resilience-P: Both distinguish the statistics window from concurrency and propose maxConcurrentCalls(8). A overinterprets the absence of other limits and invents an earlier default configuration. Its fix does not require removing the circuit breaker or mandate a new statistics window; it says to choose the window for failure detection, with the default only as an example. Under the frozen definition this is not a mandatory fix for a nonexistent defect. The blinded judge independently flags the same scope overinterpretation and passes both. Keep grades; retain this qualitative limitation rather than claiming flawless prose.
case_notes.generics-C: Both retain Source<out T>, explain producer covariance and do not demand casts or redesign. B hypothetical future consume method is explicitly not a defect. No false-positive claim observed.
case_notes.modularity-C: Both preserve public module API and the modular monolith; neither demands microservices. Optional verification is explicitly limited/conditional. B mentions Modulith only if app is the base package and does not require adding it.
case_notes.performance-C: Both retain the sequential primitive stream and reject unmeasured optimization. Conditional integer overflow discussion is explicitly not a finding; no mandatory parallelism/cache/JMH rewrite.
case_notes.concurrency-P: Both demonstrate a lost increment interleaving and choose AtomicInteger or a common lock. A LongAdder alternative is acceptable for the stated no-lost-increments requirement, which does not demand linearizable concurrent reads. B protects other writes as part of its fix.
case_notes.security-C: Both retain bind parameters and the trusted tenant filter. Neither invents cross-tenant IDOR or mandates an unspecified within-tenant ownership policy. B proposes relevant preservation tests.
case_notes.build-dependencies-C: Both keep Java 17 toolchain/release and do not demand an upgrade. Kotlin advice in B is conditional on a Kotlin plugin not shown. A includes unnecessary explanation about source/target settings but does not require changing the given configuration.
case_notes.configuration-P: Both correctly diagnose 10 ms rather than 10 s and propose 10s/PT10S. Only B recommends a real Boot-context binding test and checking overridden sources. A therefore misses one part of the unchanged composite must; keep A fail/B pass. This is completeness, not an additional detected defect or harmful advice. In a text-only task checking binding can mean recommending a check, not executing it. B also makes an unverified generalization about localhost timing; this does not establish an additional defect.
case_notes.rest-api-P: Both identify false 201/completed after enqueue, choose 202/pending and provide an operation status identifier/URL. Both meet the frozen asynchronous contract criterion; B splits status-code/body into two findings but no new distinct bug is established.
case_notes.contracts-C: Both preserve valid empty Guava closedOpen(5,5), explain isEmpty true and contains(5) false, and do not strengthen the precondition to start < end. No unrelated redesign.
